Jordan / team — attaching a concise redline summary and the exhibit we propose as a compromise that should be acceptable to both sides. High-level legal positions:

- Audit scope: we propose a "bounded sampling" approach rather than unfettered inspection; sampling cadence described in the attached redline limits requests to two sampled requests per rolling 12-month period unless escalation/incident.
- Evidence turnaround: we can commit to providing logged artifacts and SOC2 attachments within 7 business days for standard evidence requests; for privileged or forensic requests we propose a mutually-agreed plan with a reasonable extension clause (not to exceed 21 business days).
- Pen-test: Redwood supports third-party pen tests. We prefer tests be run against a staging environment where possible; if production is requested, Redwood will require 72-hour advance notice, an approved test plan, scoped blast radius, and a signing of a test-waiver addendum.
- Confidentiality & data handling: redline includes explicit handling for any customer-submitted payloads during tests (sensitive data redaction; ephemeral logs).

I've attached the redline PDF (Redwood_Security_Exhibit_Redline_v1.pdf) and summarized inline changes. We are flexible on the inspection cadence if NovaMed's compliance team has operational constraints.

Next steps: please confirm if the 72-hour production notice + staging-preference approach is acceptable and whether the 7-business-day evidence SLA meets you halfway on audit turnaround. If yes, we'll produce a clean exhibit and a final order-form addendum for signature.

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the redline, Karthik. A few operational clarifications from Security / Ops that I want to capture so the exhibit doesn't create impossible requests down the line:

- SOC2: Redwood has a rolling SOC 2 Type II report; we can share the last two periods and a pointer for continuous monitoring dashboards where available (we'll provide a link and a one-page summary). I put the SOC2 download link in the attachments (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_Link.txt).
- Evidence cadence: suggest we formalize an "evidence lane" process — standard (non-privileged) evidence requests answered within 7 business days; emergency/forensic requests routed via our incident response runbook with a max 15-business-day SLA for a full package. This gives customers predictability and protects against ad-hoc wide-scope asks.
- Pen-test ops: prefer staging for active exploit testing. If NovaMed insists on production, we require: 1) 72-hour notice; 2) signed pen-test addendum; 3) a mutually-agreed blast-radius and rollback plan; 4) Redwood on-call engineer during the window. We can support a 2-week staging window every quarter for scheduled tests (ops will provision ephemeral environments).

- Logs & retention: we'll provide redacted logs relevant to the test scope; production log exports may include pseudonymized request ids and will exclude any other tenant data. Retention and access controls are spelled out in the proposed exhibit.

Proposed schedule to meet NovaMed procurement:
- Mon 2/23 — Redwood sends clean exhibit PDF + short redline memo
- Tue 3/2 — target to return signed order form (per your procurement timeline)

If that aligns, Ben / Connor can provide an ops runbook stub for the staging flow and escalation contacts.
